seo.title: FLUX 3 Video Generator: Frames, Images and Extension
seo.description: Plan FLUX 3 Video text, image, first-and-last-frame and extension workflows with exact input boundaries, production prompting and canonical mode pricing.

overview: FLUX 3 Video is the current production route in the new FLUX video family. It supports prompt-only generation, opening-image animation, exact first-and-last-frame guidance and source-video extension. Black Forest Labs owns FLUX; MaxVideoAI distributes these launch endpoints through Fal rather than a direct Black Forest Labs route.

hero.title: FLUX 3 Video
hero.subtitle: Create from text or an image, bridge exact first and last frames, or extend a short source clip at 720p or 1080p.
hero.paragraph: Choose FLUX 3 when a production brief needs one of four explicit workflows. First-and-last-frame mode requires both anchors; extend mode requires an eligible source video and uses its own canonical rate facts. Black Forest Labs owns the model family, while Fal distributes MaxVideoAI execution for this launch.

features.title: Four explicit generation modes
features.body: Text, image, first-and-last-frame and extension each keep their own required inputs. The product does not rename keyframes or draft enhancement as generic supported modes.

features.title: Exact frame bridge
features.body: First-and-last-frame mode requires both a start and end image. Design compatible anchors and describe the motion that can plausibly connect them within five to twenty seconds.

features.title: Source-video extension
features.body: Extend accepts a short supported source clip. Continue its camera vector, subject trajectory, light and rhythm instead of restarting the scene with unrelated direction.

features.title: Separate extension quote
features.body: The canonical calculator selects extension-specific pricing facts when mode is extend. A page scenario cannot quietly reuse the less expensive normal-generation rate.

decisionCards.title: Best fit: controlled production transitions
decisionCards.body: Use FLUX 3 for product movement, designed frame bridges, source-video continuation and scene work that benefits from explicit input ownership.

decisionCards.title: Not ideal: low-cost exploratory batches
decisionCards.body: When a team is still testing many directions at 720p, use Draft as the iteration sibling and reserve standard FLUX 3 for the selected brief.

decisionCards.title: Prompt the transition, not two posters
decisionCards.body: For frame bridging, explain how pose, camera, materials and light evolve between anchors. Impossible geometry makes a stable connection less likely.

referenceWorkflows.title: Text generation
referenceWorkflows.body: Define a compact scene, physical action, camera path and stable ending.

referenceWorkflows.title: Image animation
referenceWorkflows.body: Protect the opening composition and direct movement without redesigning the source.

referenceWorkflows.title: First and last frames
referenceWorkflows.body: Supply both required images and describe a physically plausible path between them.

referenceWorkflows.title: Video extension
referenceWorkflows.body: Use an eligible source clip and continue its established motion, camera, identity and atmosphere.

tabNotes.body: The canonical launch supports fl2v, not a generic keyframe sequence with arbitrary intermediate frames.
Start and end images should share compatible subject identity, perspective and scene logic.
Extend pricing is mode-specific, and the source clip must satisfy the published format, size and length rules.

globalPrinciples: Choose a mode before composing the prompt.
Make movement physically compatible with source media.
Use one motivated camera path per short scene.
Review rights, consent, safety, unintended text and watermarks before approval.
engineWhy: FLUX 3 separates first-last-frame control from ordinary image animation.
A dedicated extension route preserves source-video ownership and pricing context.
Standard output supports 720p and 1080p for review and production decisions.

demo.title: FLUX 3 first-last-frame bridge
demo.prompt: Begin from the supplied wide frame of a red fabric installation hanging motionless in a white gallery. A gentle airflow lifts the lower panels in sequence while the camera tracks slowly right. Transition naturally into the supplied final close frame where the fabric curves around a polished steel form. Preserve gallery geometry, fabric color and light direction. No visitors, signs or logos.
notes: The prompt names the physical force and compatible camera path.
Both anchors share a location, material and lighting logic.
